content.comment_body: Is it possible for example: I1 button toggles Q1 on/off, I2 button toggles Q2 on/off, and I3 button controls both Q1 and Q2 together for on/off? Thanks, but I can't figure it out.
Yes, that's possible. I1, I2, and I3 should be push buttons (normally open). When you use I3 within one second: pressing I3 once turns Q1 and Q2 on, pressing I3 twice turns Q1 and Q2 off.
Thanks, but is it possible to implement this table logic for three push buttons and two outputs using [product_name] V8? I'm unable to do it.
This solution isn't easy for me to use in a home automation setup, especially without a signal lamp on the button. Even with a signal lamp, it's difficult.

The logic table you provided doesn't make sense, especially considering the thread's topic. My friend [user_name] offered a sensible solution earlier. Could you clarify what devices you are physically connecting to Q1 and Q2, as well as to I1, I2, and I3? Please describe what you want to achieve. Even a photo of your electrical layout would help. We need more details to assist you. Thank you.
For the logic table, the second example is correct.
I1 starts Q1 light, I1 stops Q1 light. I2 starts Q2 light, I2 stops Q2 light. I3 controls logic according to the table.

If I1, I2, and I3 are buttons, the first suggested approach is correct. If they are switches, then the second suggested method works. If buttons are used, your logic table doesn't match the intended behavior.

Hello. Showing a picture of the system would be very helpful. Even without an image, please describe your design intentions. Check the attached file. Keep in mind, the system will only execute the requested action after releasing a button, since the PLC cannot know the user's intent without this. Test the program and let us know if anything isn't working for you. Apologies for not making the documentation very detailed or the circuit diagram more readable. Greetings.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are attempting to set up a multi-button circuit using [product_name] V8 for home automation, but face challenges with understanding both the logic design and the actual wiring. Clarifying the operation of push buttons vs. switches and providing clear documentation or diagrams is seen as helpful for troubleshooting and implementation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a simple and clear system for controlling multiple outputs with several buttons, which is easy to set up and understand for home use. They expect straightforward logic and practical guidance for implementation.
